authors: Pengju Liu (Katie), Nuo Xu (Katie), Winso Chen (Katie), Peijun Li (Katie),  Yang (Katie),  Zhao, Yu Cao, Caiwen Ding
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.31876v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Design Rule Checking (DRC) error fixing remains a time-consuming bottleneck in physical design, often requiring manual intervention despite advanced EDA optimizations. Existing LLM-agent approaches fall short due to redundant contextual shapes, limited spatial reasoning over raw coordinates, and inefficient flat layout representations. We propose AgentDRC, which formulates iterative DRC correction as a multi-agent algorithm and introduces a spatial-aware verification and correction algorithm that reconstructs structured spatial relations among critical shapes and validates fixes through geometric and semantic constraint checking. papers.title: Power Side-Channel Evaluation using Multi-FPGA Systems
authors: Yaswanth Tavva, Geng Luo, Trevor E. Carlson, Li-Shiuan Peh
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.32652v1 Announce Type: cross 
Abstract: Complex out-of-order processors are difficult to evaluate for power side-channel leakage before tapeout. A single FPGA often lacks sufficient capacity, whereas conventional CAD-based analysis is too slow to support the large numbers of traces required by practical attacks. Multi-FPGA emulation provides greater capacity, but existing partitioning schemes are not security-aware and thus results in poor attack performance. This work presents Scissors, a security-aware multi-FPGA partitioning approach for pre-silicon power side-channel evaluation of complex out-of-order processors. papers.title: ExitLUT: Boolean Early Exits for Efficient FPGA-Based Neural Network Inference
authors: Oliver Cassidy, Marta Andronic, George A. Constantinides
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.31540v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Early exit neural networks reduce average inference cost by terminating once sufficient confidence is reached. On FPGAs, conventional confidence-based exits add arithmetic control paths poorly matched to LUT fabrics, consuming resources that could otherwise support the main datapath. We present ExitLUT, which replaces softmax-style exit decisions with learned Boolean functions mapped directly into FPGA LUTs. In our CNN evaluation, fpgaConvNet is the static spatial-dataflow baseline, while ATHEENA is its softmax-based early exit extension. ExitLUT reduces ATHEENA's exit-decision LUT usage by 2.58$\times$ over the softmax path and eliminates decision-path DSP usage, while preserving accuracy and exit behavior. papers.title: OpenWoud: Vendor-Unlocked Scalable Adaptive Random Forest Accelerator
authors: Ewout van Nimwegen, Elijah Seth Cishugi, Hendrik Folmer, Marco Ottavi, Kuan-Hsun Chen
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.32662v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Online Machine Learning (ML) enables real-time decision-making on evolving data streams. These dynamic models learn continuously to adapt to new concepts, as previous ones become invalid, but their performance is often limited by throughput. The Adaptive Random Forest (ARF) is a state-of-the-art model for this setting, which naturally exposes parallelism and is therefore well-suited for hardware acceleration. However, prior Field Programmable Gate Array (FPGA)-based accelerators are vendor-locked and rely on resource-hungry Floating-Point (FP) arithmetics, limiting their scalability and portability. papers.title: On the Design of a Slow Control Interlock System for the European GateMate FPGA
authors: Vitalii Burtsev, Daniele Passaretti, Daniel Anders, Christof Pfannenmueller, Fabian Lurz, Thilo Pionteck
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.32275v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Slow Control Systems (SCSs) are essential for the monitoring, configuration, and protection of distributed safety-critical systems in scientific, industrial, and medical applications. Although software-based SCS architectures offer flexibility and scalability, they suffer from software aging and non-deterministic latencies, which limit long-term reliability and timely reaction to critical errors, often requiring additional hardware interlock systems. This paper presents an FPGA-centric lightweight Slow Control Interlock System (SCIS) designed to achieve deterministic ultra-low-latency reaction times in long-running dependable systems. papers.title: Trading BRAM for LUTs: Hybrid Bit-Level Weight Storage for FPGA-Based Spiking Neural Networks
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.32288v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) offer an attractive paradigm for energy-efficient AI inference, while their deployment on reconfigurable hardware enables application-specific acceleration without sacrificing model reprogrammability. However, realizing this potential on FPGAs is often severely constrained by the immense on-chip memory needed to store synaptic weights. Existing compression techniques reduce this storage requirement at the cost of weight precision or accuracy. This work presents a hybrid bit-level weight-storage scheme that trades BRAM capacity for FPGA logic resources while preserving the original weights unmodified. papers.title: Mayfly: Lifecycle-Aware High-Bandwidth Flash for Recursive Self-Improvement
authors: Chunlin Tian, Mingjia Fan, Feng Yu, Qingyun Zou, Wenju Zhao, Weng-Fai Wong, Bingsheng He
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.32264v1 Announce Type: new 
Abstract: Recursive self-improvement (RSI) lets an LLM improve its agent system by proposing and evaluating candidate variants across tasks. A generation's sessions grow their KV caches together and release them as they finish, creating a burst followed by a decline. At high concurrency, even the KV of sessions ready to run exceeds the GPU's HBM. Offloading that KV to host DRAM or SSDs adds capacity but leaves ready sessions waiting for HBM space before execution. High-Bandwidth Flash (HBF) can serve the overflow in place, but excessive reads lengthen decode steps and repeated writes consume flash endurance. papers.title: Hypnos: A Dual-Phase End-to-End Platform for Scalable Continual Learning at the Edge
authors: Guilherme Guedes, Marco P. Apolinario, Charlotte Frenkel
papers.abstract:
arXiv:2611.24637v3 Announce Type: replace 
Abstract: Continual learning (CL) enables neural networks to adapt to non-stationary data streams by mitigating catastrophic forgetting, offering a path to robust, private, and adaptable edge devices. Yet, porting CL to real-world edge devices remains challenging for two reasons: (i) online operation, where sensor data arrives one sample at a time and the device must adapt on-the-fly, and (ii) the low footprint of edge devices, which makes traditional error backpropagation training prohibitive.
